name: Verdant Labs Contamination Handler Gloves
description:
Elbow-length gloves made from multi-layered barrier material that resists chemical, biological, and radiological contamination. The outer layer is self-sealing — small punctures close within seconds. A color-change indicator strip along each finger shifts from green to red when the barrier integrity is compromised.

Used in hazmat operations, substrate containment, and illegal pharmaceutical manufacturing. The self-sealing feature means a single pair can survive conditions that would destroy standard protective equipment.
functionality: Chemical/biological/radiological barrier, self-sealing punctures, integrity monitoring
what_it_says: Whatever you're touching would kill you through your skin if these gloves weren't between you and it.
story_hooks: A discarded pair of Contamination Handler gloves tests positive for a substance that doesn't match any known chemical compound — whatever was handled in these gloves hasn't been catalogued yet.

physical_description.visual_profile: Clinical yet imposing — elbow-length gauntlets with a sleek, purposeful silhouette. The gloves taper slightly at the wrist and flare subtly at the forearm, creating a pseudo-tactical aesthetic. When worn, they read as heavy-duty medical or industrial protective gear, commanding respect and unease in equal measure.
physical_description.fit: Compression-fitted through the palm and fingers with a relaxed, articulated forearm section. The elasticized cuff sits snug at the elbow crease without restricting movement. Designed for prolonged wear and repeated contact.
physical_description.primary_material: Multi-layered synthetic barrier composite — likely polychloroprene or proprietary bio-resistant polymer blend. The outer layer has a subtle pearlescent sheen from the self-sealing micromesh matrix. Inner lining is soft, moisture-wicking treated fabric.
physical_description.texture: Outer surface is smooth and slightly tacky to the touch, with microscopic dimpling where the self-sealing matrix lies. Inner forearm feels almost velvety. Seams are triple-stitched and reinforced with sealed tape.
physical_description.color_scheme: Pale clinical white or pale gray base with bright acid-green indicator strips running the length of each finger and along the knuckles. Verdant Labs branding in dark teal or forest green at the wrist cuff.
physical_description.closures: Elastic compression cuff at the elbow with a subtle friction-lock adjustment tab. Some variants feature magnetic micro-snaps for quick removal without contamination spread.
distinctive_features: Color-change indicator strips (green-to-red) on each finger and knuckle ridge
Self-sealing outer layer with visible micromesh texture
Reinforced fingertip grip panels with micro-texture
Interior wrist anchor loop to prevent bunching
Printed batch code and expiration date on inner forearm
Asymmetrical padding at palm heel and thumb joint for durability
Verdant Labs corporate logo embossed at wrist cuff
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2-3 crossover. Expensive enough to signal professional/corporate use (Tier 2 safety infrastructure), but widely distributed to working-class hazmat crews and black-market pharmaceutical ops (Tier 3). Street price: 800-1200 Φ per pair.
physical_description.cultural_context: Wearing these gloves signals expertise in contamination handling — whether that's legitimate Verdant Labs subsidiary work, independent hazmat contracting, or underground biotech operations. They're a flex in dangerous spaces. Possession alone in certain jurisdictions triggers security protocols.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine when fresh from the package with visible indicator green. Broken-in pairs show wear on the fingertips and palm heel, with slight discoloration from repeated exposure to solvents or biological matter. Heavy-use gloves may have small sealed punctures visible as faint scar lines on the outer layer.
